page: Amazon Web Services c7i.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs and 4 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the c7i.2xlarge demonstrates strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 32.73 GB/sec and text processing with a Geekbench score of 2743.0, both placing in the top 25% tier. General CPU capabilities are solid, with a Passmark CPU score of 13119.77 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7695.0, both aligning with average tier performance. However, memory-bound workloads show some limitations; the Passmark memory score of 1800.86 falls into the bottom 25% tier, and uncached large-block memory read and write speeds are measured at 47.98 GB/sec and 44.81 GB/sec respectively. Large-model LLM text generation is also limited, with the 7B model achieving 6.32 tokens/sec.

Given its compute-to-memory ratio of 1:2 and the lack of bundled local storage, the c7i.2xlarge offers a resource-dense profile optimized for CPU-bound tasks rather than memory-intensive databases. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that leverage its specialized Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets, such as lightweight machine learning inference, cryptography, and vector calculations. Suitable workloads include software compilation, web serving, text processing, and moderate computational tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or local SSD storage.
